correctness.rationale: Reconstructed input monomial moments v_n=int_0^1 t^n w(t)dt and orthonormal-coordinate operator K_{mn}=1/[(m+n+1)sqrt((m+1)v_n)]. Laplace substitution gives v_n=(log n)^2 a(loglog n)^2/n (1+O(1/log n)), using bounded positive a and bounded derivative; tail effects integrated against e^-y. The low triangular m>n and upper m<=n error squared sums between K and P_d, P_{mn}=1_(n>=m)/(sqrt(mn) log n), d_n=1/a(loglog n), are finite since sum 1/(n log²n)<infty. A Schur weight h_n=(n log n)^(-1/2) gives essential norm <=2 for P; weakly null loglog coordinate windows produce lower norm approaching 2. For P_d upper <=2 limsup d and lower use a_prime->0 to keep d nearly constant over each fixed additive u-window, then send window width to infinity. The example has liminf a=3/4 and derivative tending to zero, giving 8/3. Independent approximate finite-window Copson integral singular values for lengths 4,8,16,32 approached 2 with expected coarse-grid bias; not cited as proof of infinite essential norm.
residual_risks: Exact result is an essential norm between two different Bergman spaces, not the unweighted coefficient operator norm nor Fredholm spectrum.
Slow derivative and uniform positive bounds essential to the localized lower bound; rapid oscillations or liminf zero excluded.
Numerical finite windows do not certify the infinite-dimensional norm.
